Use case: style-transfer.
Edit target Image1 is our NEW independent black-ground single-board PBR albedo, not a photograph. Image2 is ONLY a temple-ceiling style/detail reference, never source pixels for the material or a room image.
Keep the portrait3:5 flat panel, very deep quiet blue-black ground, restrained warm old-gold pigment palette, tiny brush texture, and orthographic uniformly unlit surface nature of Image1. Change only the painted ornament: replace the large broad eight-petaled flower and four oversized corner blooms entirely. Author a noticeably finer, more compact ROUND lotus/chrysanthemum/hosoge medallion, about60-65% of the panel WIDTH, with three nested whorls of many small rounded petal tips, fine stamens, tiny hand-painted gold veins and little leaf lobes. It must read as delicate intricate classical Japanese Buddhist ceiling painting, not a thick-petaled logo or a radial geometric mandala. Add four much smaller restrained corner lotus/cloud-leaf sprays with fine gold outlines and small filled petals, each about22-27% of panel width. Preserve generous quiet black ground around and between the discrete motifs. Fine light-old-gold linework and muted ochre pigment, not large bright solid yellow or orange shapes; no ivory/white petals. No long winding wallpaper vines, no Western Rococo acanthus, no vector icon look, no parchment dirt or broad crackle.
The whole canvas remains JUST ONE independent flat painted material surface. No border or timber frame, no bevel or embossing, no perspective, no room or ceiling view, no cast or contact shadows, no specular highlights, no gold glints, no lighting gradient, bloom, emission or glowing lines, no text/seals/logos. Paint color only, to be lit later on real closed wooden boards by ordinary PBR in a separately modeled3D room. Never reproduce any photographic geometry or illumination from Image2. Keep all previous variants separate.
